 p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text" data-subscriber-content> It’s finally election day and you’re ready to head to the polls to cast you r ballot in California’s 2026 midterm, but you don’t know where the nearest polling location is. Or perhaps you misplaced your ballot.
 Here are some common last-minute election-day hiccups and how to navigate them so you can earn your “I voted” sticker on Tuesday. 
 I forgot to register to vote
 You can still register as a conditional voter on election day through the “same day” voter registration process. 
 Advertisement Eligible citizens who need to register or re-register to vote within 14 days of an election can complete this process at county elections offices, polling places or vote centers.
 If you’ve become a U.S. citizen fewer than 15 days before the election, you may register to vote by visiting your county elections office anytime before the polls close on election day. You must bring proof that you are a U.S. citizen and sign a form saying you are eligible to vote in California.
 For all those registering, the application requires a state driver’s license or California identification card number, or you can use the last four digits of your Social Security card.
 Advertisement If you don’t have any of those, you can still register. You’ll be assigned a unique identifier to validate your registration.
 With same-day registration, you are “conditionally” registered to vote, and your ballot is provisional. Once officials have confirmed you are registered to vote in that county, your ballot is then processed and counted. 
 I don’t know where my polling place is
 You can look for the nearest polling place by entering your address in the “Find your polling place” tool on the California secretary of state’s website. 
 The Los Angeles County office of the registrar-recorder/county clerk has a vote center locator that includes the wait time to cast your ballot. 
 I’m here at the polling place but forgot my ballot at home
 You can request a provisional ballot at any polling place in the county in which you are registered to vote. 
 A provisional ballot is a regular ballot that is placed in a special envelope prior to being put in the ballot box. 
 Advertisement It’s counted once election officials verify that you are a registered voter in that county and haven’t already voted in the election. 
 I can’t submit my mail-in ballot myself
 You can have someone else submit your ballot.
 Anyone can drop off your mailed ballot as long as you authorize them to do so and they do not get paid on a per-ballot basis, according to the secretary of state .
 You and the person you’ve authorized to submit your mailed ballot must fill out and sign the outside of the ballot envelope.
 I forgot my check-in code for in-person voting
 Los Angeles County election officials say you can check in at a vote center by scanning your “quick check-in code” — a number that verifies your voter registration.
 Your unique code can be found on your mailed sample ballot and vote center postcard. Take either of those hard copies to the vote center.
 If you forgot the hard copies, you can find the code online. You retrieve it by verifying your voter registration here . You’ll need to input your last name, birth date, the house number of your residential address and your ZIP Code. For assistance call, (800) 815-2666, Option 2.
 Advertisement I’ve heard about touch-screen voting machines not working
 It’s a common issue: You touch your voting machine screen, and it doesn’t show your intended selection.
 Election officials say touch-screen challenges are commonly caused by user error or an easily fixed screen miscalibration .
 Flag a poll worker if you’re having difficulty. If you’ve already printed a ballot that doesn’t reflect your intended selections, don’t cast it; notify a poll worker who will follow procedures for replacing the ballot.
 How late is too late to put my ballot in a ballot box?
 There are three ways you can submit your mailed ballot on election day:
 You can put it in a ballot drop box. The cutoff time to do so is the same time that polls close, 8 p.m.
 Drop it off at a polling place, vote center or county elections office by 8 p.m.
 Drop it off at a United States post office. To ensure your ballot is postmarked by election day, mail it at least by Thursday — five days before Tuesday’s election. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee at a U.S. post office.
 Where is my nearest ballot box?
 The Los Angeles County registrar-recorder/county clerk’s office has an online tool here to help you find a ballot box near you.
 I think I forgot to sign my mailed ballot envelope
 If you turned in your vote-by-mail ballot and forgot to sign it, your vote will still count. 
 Your county elections official will notify you by mail, phone or email. You can also be notified by way of the “Where’s My Ballot?” tracking tool, which offers automatic notifications that will ping you if there are issues with your ballot.
 Advertisement To remedy the issue, your county elections office will provide you with a form to fill out and return completed.
 The form will be given to you two days prior to the day your county certifies the election, so be sure to fill it out and return it to your county elections office right away.
 How late is too late to vote at the polls on election night?
 In California, any voter who is in line at 8 p.m. when the polls are scheduled to close is allowed to vote, according to the secretary of state .
 If there is a line when the polls close, a poll worker stands at the back of the line to let people who arrive after 8 p.m. know that the polls have closed.
 Any voter who arrives after the polls have closed may not be allowed to vote, even if voters who were in line to vote before the polls closed are in the process of voting.
